: JUDGMENT :

The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB / NH-7 /
CR / 10 / 2017-18 dated 14.07.2021 pertaining to Sy. No.43/1 measuring 2811.91 Sq. feet of Shivanahalli A.P. No.197/2021 village, Bengaluru North Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District.
.2.

The definite case of the petitioner is that the property bearing Sy. No.43/1 measuring 2811.91 Sq.
feet of Shivanahalli village, Bengaluru North Taluka, Bengaluru, belonging to the respondent No.1 and that has been acquired under Preliminary Notification under Section 3A(1) vide S.O. No.3159 (E) dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification under Section 3D(1) and (2) vide S.O. No. 1874(E)
dated 30.07.2010.

The respondent No.3 has passed the award on 22.02.2011 determined the market value of NA lands at Rs. 1,389/- per Sq. feet and in total a sum of Rs.39,05,743/- has been awarded as compensation and the said amount has been disbursed to the respondent No.1.
The respondent No.1 received the said amount under protest and filed an application on 15.12.2017 for enhancing the compensation claiming at the rate of Rs. 10,000/- per Sq. feet.
Accordingly, the said application is taken by the respondent No. 2 for consideration.

In the said petition/proceedings before the respondent No.2, this petitioner filed statement of objections stating that the application filed by the petitioner for reference is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
The respondent No. 1 has not produced any documents for enhancing the compensation.

Further, it is claimed by the petitioner that the proper compensation has been awarded by the respondent No.3 and claimed that the respondent No. 3 has awarded excess amount than the market value of the property under Preliminary Notification.
The petitioner in the objection statement also stated about the provisions of law and case Laws and prayed for dismissal of the reference.
.4. Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an enquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR- 11/10/2017-18 dated 14.07.2021.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section A.P. No.197/2021 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting up the following :

:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the impugned award passed by the respondent No. 2 is perverse, patently illegal, capricious and goes against the very fundamentals of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
The respondent No.2 ought to have rejected the claims of the respondent No.1 since the claim of the respondent No.1 was barred by time.

The respondent No.2 without adjudicating the aspect of limitation could not have proceeded to award enhancement and the impugned Arbitral Award on the face of it is erroneous rending the same patently illegal.
The respondent No.2 instead of following the view of a party to the proceedings ought to have applied mind to the existing position of law by bringing the said letter to the notice of the parties.

Even assuming without admitting that the application under Section 3-G(5) was not barred by limitation, the market value A.P. No.197/2021 determined by the respondent No.2 is contrary to the provisions of NH Act and the Arbitration and Conciliation Act and so far as redetermination of market value is concerned, the respondent No.2 ought to have followed Section 3-G(7)(a) of the NH Act.

The respondent No.3 has rightly determined the market value by taking into consideration both the sale statistics as well as the guidance value for the relevant period and there was no scope for interference with the same.

The respondent No.2 has grossly erred in not following the provisions of NH Act i.e., Section 3-G(7)(a) the substantive law while passing the impugned award which is contrary to the provisions of Section 28 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

The respondent No.2 has held that the guidance value of NA lands situated at the said village which are abutting the left side of Jakkur Aerodrome to Kogilu Bypass road coming within the jurisdiction of Yelahanka CMC limits was Rs.3,000/- per Sq. feet under the aforesaid notification dated 21.09.2011 A.P.
No.197/2021 and the Arbitrator has added 40% on the guidance value by holding that the subject lands are NA Commercial in nature and arrived at the rate of Rs.4,200/-
per Sq. feet i.e., Rs. 3,000/- per Sq. feet + Rs. 1,200/- (40% of Rs. 3,000) = Rs.
4200/- per Sq. feet.
Among other grounds, prayed to allow the petition as prayed.
.6. The respondent No.1 filed Objection claiming that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
The respondent No.1 admitted the acquisition of land and passing of the award as claimed in the petition.

The respondent No. 1 in his detailed objection denied the para wise written statements and claimed that the Arbitrator /
respondent No. 2 by appreciating acquired land the material on record properly enhanced the compensation and there is no material placed by the petitioner to interfere with the order of respondent No. 2 and parcel of this statement of and accordingly prayed to dismiss the petition.

The respondent No. 1 to 3 though served with the notice, the respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel, the respondents 2 and 3 not chosen National Highway Authority Of India vs Avinash Y S on 4 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76275755/
3 to appear before this Court to resist the petition and hence, the respondents 2 and 3 have been placed exparte.

.8. On the basis of above, the points for consideration are as under:
1) Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?
2) What order or award?
.9.
Heard the arguments.

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the affirmative Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following:
A.P. No.197/2021 REASONS .10. POINT No.1: Before proceeding further in this case,
it is relevant to note admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondent No.1 Y.S. Avinash is an owner of the property bearing Sy. No. 43/1 measuring 2811.91 Square feet of Shivanahalli village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-7 under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 30.07.2010
is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.3/Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the market value of NA lands at Rs.1,389/- per Square feet for the acquired land.

sentences.text:
It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.39,05,743/-
was disbursed to the respondent No. 1 as compensation.

.11. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the respondent No. 1 Y.S. Avinash filed an application before the respondent No. 2 A.P.
No.197/2021 claiming that he is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs. 10,000/-
per Square feet as on 15.12.2017.

On the basis of said application, the respondent No.
2 held an enquiry and passed order in LAQ / ARB / NH-7 / CR / 11 / 10 / 2017-18 dated 14.07.2021.

The respondent No. 2 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs. 4,200/- per Square feet i.e., Rs. 3,000/- per Square feet + Rs. 1,200/- (40% of Rs.
3,000/-) by adding Rs.1389/- to the compensation decided by the respondent No. 3 i.e., Rs. 2,811/- per Square feet.
.12. The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No. 2 without considering the relevant provisions of National Highways Authority Act and also without considering the guidance value or market value of the property as on the date of Preliminary Notification enhanced the compensation by relying on the guidance value of the year 2010-11 published vide notification bearing No. CVC/19/2010-11 dated 21.09.2011 National Highway Authority Of India vs Avinash Y S on 4 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76275755/
4 and the said A.P. No.197/2021 document is not part of arbitration proceedings.

sentences.text: The petitioner also claimed that the decision of the respondent No.1 was based on the said notification is without knowledge of the petitioner and said guidance value of the year 2010-11 has not been brought to the notice of the petitioner.
Accordingly, claimed that such award is liable to be set aside as per Section 24 of National Highways Authority Act.

In this context, the petitioner relied on the decision reported in (2019)
15 SCC 131 in a case of Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India.

entities.text: Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is true that in the said decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that whatever the document relied by the Arbitrator shall be brought to the notice of the parties, so that the parties can make submission or give a rebuttal evidence about such documents.

Hence, it is necessary to see whether such notification is found in the records received by the Arbitrator /
respondent No.2.
On perusal of entire records of the arbitration proceedings, it is nowhere A.P. No.197/2021 discloses about the obtaining of notification by the respondent No. 2 before proceeding to pass the award.
Further, who has produced the said notification dated 21.09.2011 regarding guidance value of the year 2010- 11, is also not forth-coming.
In-fact, there is no material on record to show that such notification is there bearing No. CVC/19/2010-11 dated 21.09.2011 issued by the Stamp and Registration Department.
In the entire order, nowhere discloses that the Arbitrator has brought the said notification to the knowledge of the petitioner.
In-fact, no document is found, which substantiate the enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Arbitrator.
.13. The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No.2 without any application of mind, has allowed the claim of respondent No.1 in part and has enhanced the compensation from Rs.1,389/- per Square feet to Rs.
4,200/- per Square feet and thereby redetermining the A.P. No.197/2021 market value at 300% of the amount awarded by the respondent No.2.
.14.

In this context, the Advocate for the petitioner submitted that enhanced rate is not in accordance with the estimated market value of the immovable properties and buildings as per the notification No. CVC/19/2010-11 Bengaluru dated 21.09.2011.

It is stated that as per the guidance value the estimated market value or guidance value for the property at Shivanahalli is at Rs. 1,200/-
per Sq. feet for converted sites as well as sites situates within the limits of CMC and Rs. 1,000/- per Sq. feet ff the property situated in gramathana.

Similarly Rs. 225 lakhs fixed for agricultural land and building with Mosaic / Ceramic Vitrified tiles the rate is fixed at Rs. 1630/- per Sq. feet and the building with marble / granite tiles the rate is fixed at Rs. 1760/- per Sq. feet.
On perusal of order, it is clear that the rate of enhancement fixed by the Arbitrator per Sq. feet is at Rs. 2811/- which is certainly contrary to the guidance A.P. No.197/2021 value.
Hence, this Court is liable to be intervened with the award and the award is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the above point is held in the affirmative.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Section 34 (2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act,
1996 is hereby allowed.
